query: What signals in a travel-expense description predict whether it will be declined?

per_column.name: is_travel
per_column.rationale: Binary flag for whether the expense is travel-related, derivable from the description. Well-separated categories (354/146) and interpretable; a human can segment declined rates by travel vs non-travel, directly serving the query's focus on travel-expense descriptions.

per_column.name: has_automated_desc
per_column.rationale: Flags automated/boilerplate descriptions, an external associational signal in the text. Reasonably balanced (381/119) and interpretable; one can compare decline rates between automated and human-written descriptions, a plausible signal for declines.

per_column.name: is_high_amount
per_column.rationale: Discretizes amount into high/low, giving a clean two-way segmentation (264/236) that a human can group on and compare against decline rate. Interpretable scale-derived category, not opaque.

per_column.name: missing_processing
per_column.rationale: Flags absence of processing data, an interpretable and well-separated category (295/205). Could plausibly associate with declines and supports meaningful grouping, though it is more procedural than a description signal per se.

judge.rationale: All four added columns are external, associational binary flags with well-separated, interpretable categories that a human can group on and compare against state_declined, satisfying the EDA claim. None merely restate the focus, and none are near-constant or opaque scores. The set is moderately strong for discovering interpretable relationships: is_travel and has_automated_desc are genuine description-derived signals aligned with the query, is_high_amount is a clean amount segmentation. Informativeness is held below the top range because the columns are all coarse binary buckets (limiting granularity of exploration) and missing_processing is more of a data-pipeline artifact than a substantive description signal, so the set covers a fairly narrow slice of potentially informative relationships.
